Bridge Michigan: the Michigan Republican Party spent $1.8 million on ads supporting John James; filings trace the money to Dan and Douglas DeVos, who gave $2 million on Oct 19 and 20 to Michigan Victory 2026, a committee formed by the Republican Governors Association.
The Michigan Democratic Party filed a campaign finance complaint against the James campaign and the state GOP, arguing the arrangement exceeds state limits. The complaint is unresolved.
State law lets a party give up to $750,000 to a publicly funded gubernatorial candidate; James reported $1.9 million in total party support.
James's campaign relies on a recent U.S. Supreme Court ruling that lifted limits on federal party spending; Bridge describes the theory as untested because the ruling concerns federal limits.

WMUK: in Michigan's 4th District, mailers promote Green candidate Shafina Barnett over Democrat Sean McCann and stress opposition to data centers; the payer is Progressive Champions PAC, whose funding came 100 percent from Conservative Americans PAC, described as Republican-aligned.
Green Party of Michigan spokesperson Douglas Marsh says neither Barnett nor the party had any connection to the mailers and calls them an attempt to pull votes from Democrats.

Proposal 2 would bar regulated electric and gas utilities and government contractors with more than $250,000 in contracts, and people with substantial ties to them, from contributing to candidates who make decisions affecting them, and would extend disclosure rules to more political communications including online ads.

Developer cofounder Tom Dorris cites a $20 million community fund, six hours of battery storage and closed-loop cooling. The township manager says the township learned of the announcement when the media did and ended its membership in the Lansing Economic Area Partnership.
